endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Report GAI incidents in compliance with legal and regulatory requirements (e.g., HIPAA breach reporting, e.g., OCR (2023) or NHTSA (2022) autonomous vehicle crash reporting requirements.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Ensure AI systems are incorporated into Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BCDR) plans—the failure of a clinical AI system during an outage should be anticipated, not improvised.

endorsements.title: Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) guidance
endorsements.issuer: The Joint Commission and Coalition for Health AI
endorsements.quote: Incident Response Plan: Develop and maintain an incident response plan to address data breaches and other security incidents promptly and effectively.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Determine whether incident response plans are established, maintained, and tested according to policies for AI solutions.

endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: I ndependent of an entity’s legal responsibility to notify a health care provider or organization of a data breach, that entity should also act diligently in identifying and notifying the individuals themselves of breaches that impact their personal information.

endorsements.title: Ethical integration of patient-reported outcomes and digital biomarkers in AI healthcare models: an expert consensus framework
endorsements.quote: Establish clear notification protocols in case of security breaches or data leaks, ensuring patients are promptly informed.

endorsements.title: Multimodal generative AI for pre-practicum mental health support competency development: a human-supervised framework for education-childcare partnerships
endorsements.quote: Incident procedures specify reportable events, severity, responsibilities, containment, notification, remediation, and escalation.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether AI incident response plans, continuity plans, or breach notification practices reduce delays or harm after AI-related breaches or outages. The recommendation rests on seven endorsements, two of them framework-level "must" statements, and on existing HIPAA and state breach-notification duties rather than on outcome data.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Seven sources endorse it, including NIST AI 600-1 and CHAI playbooks at the "must" level, but endorsements are expert opinion. Under GRADE conventions, the absence of any comparative or observational test means certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence.

NIST AI 600-1 ties AI incident reporting to existing legal duties such as HIPAA breach reporting to OCR. Those duties may already apply to breaches of protected health information whether or not an AI system is involved. The notification element appears to restate current law, while the continuity-planning element rests on framework guidance.

The Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use ask entities to notify affected individuals directly, independent of any legal duty to notify a provider or organization. A consensus commentary also calls for prompt patient notification. No supplied study measures whether patients receive, understand, or act on AI-related breach notices, so the benefit to patients remains untested.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare organizations with and without AI-specific incident response and continuity plans on time to detection, time to containment, time to patient and regulator notification, and clinical disruption during AI outages. Descriptive work documenting how often AI-related breaches and outages occur in health care would also establish the size of the hazard, which no supplied study measures.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether breach notices reach and are understood by patients with limited English proficiency or low literacy, and whether safety-net systems can staff and test these plans, remains unknown.
